subject: Post-call qualification + POC sprint charter — Tactica Systems
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@tactica.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call qualification + POC sprint charter — Tactica Systems

Hi Maria & Carlos —

Thanks again for the conversation today. Quick recap so we have the same view and clear next steps to get a POC started next week. I kept this intentionally short.

Highlights / pain we heard
- High latency and token cost on nightly batch summarization pipeline (50k docs/day) causing QA backlogs and advisor delays.
- Current infra struggles with consistent latency at 99th pct due to variable sequence lengths and concurrency spikes.
- Need strict data isolation and auditability for clinical content.

Goals we aligned on
- Reduce nightly summarization cost by 40–60% while preserving extractive accuracy (ROUGE-like checks).
- Reach 95th pct latency below 700ms for query workloads in staging with burst tolerance.
- Demonstrate secure deployment that meets their audit checklist items in two weeks.

POC scope (proposed)
1) Data/sample: 10k anonymized summaries from the nightly job (we'll provide ingestion template).
2) Success metrics: cost per 1k tokens, ROUGE-1 F1 delta vs baseline, 95th/99th latency, and audit log completeness.
3) Deliverables: POC charter doc, prompt suite, prompt/eval harness, and a small ops runbook for access.
4) Duration: 2-week sprint + 1-week buffer for compliance artifacts.

Owners (suggested)
- Redwood AE (sales owner): Vivek (me) — kickoff, mutual action plan, contract coordination.
- Redwood Solutions/Platform: Karthik — access, infra config, performance tuning.
- Customer lead: Maria Lopez — data access, evaluation sign-off.

Immediate asks from Maria/Carlos
1) Share sample anonymized batch by Monday EOD (S3 link or secure Share).
2) Security questionnaire: we'll complete the provided form and return by Wednesday.
3) Confirm legal contact for an MSA/POC addendum.

Attachments: POC-Charter-Tactica-v1.pdf (outline + success metrics)

Next step: I can schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday 9–11am PT — what works for you?

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com | (415) 555-0107

[Attachment: POC-Charter-Tactica-v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@tactica.ai>

Cc: Carlos Vega <c.vega@tactica.ai>, Procurement <procurement@tactica.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call qualification + POC sprint charter — Tactica Systems

Vivek —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A few clarifications:
- We can produce a 10k sample set but it will be staggered: 3k on Monday, remaining 7k mid-week. Is that ok?
- The procurement contact is Alicia Ramos; I looped procurement above. They will handle the PO/contract.
- Attached is our security questionnaire — please mark any items you cannot meet and we can triage.

Kickoff: Monday 10am PT works for Maria, Carlos, and Alicia.

Carlos will also want a short demo of how we handle prefix caching and whether Redwood can provide a deterministic fallback for longer sequences.

I appreciate the timeline proposal — please proceed with the charter and share the DocuSign when ready.

Best,
Maria
Maria Lopez
Director of Data Products, Tactica Systems
maria.lopez@tactica.ai | +1 212-555-0188

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@tactica.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: POC kickoff plan + owners (follow-up)

Hi all —

Appreciate the quick turn. I updated the charter and playbook based on Maria's notes and added a lightweight eval plan and prompt suite. Summary of changes:
- Split data ingest into two batches as requested (ingest template in the playbook).
- Added an entry for prefix/KV cache validation and a short test harness to measure deterministic fallbacks.
- Included exact success criteria rows we will track daily in the shared sheet.

Concrete plan / timeline
Week 0 (Mon): Kickoff + access exchange; ingest batch 1 (3k).
Week 1 (Tue–Thu): Model tuning & prompt/eval runs; daily 30-min standups.
Week 2 (Mon): Ingest batch 2 (7k); finalize metrics and handoff README.
Completion (end of Week 2): Delivery of metrics report and ops runbook.

Owners & contacts
- Vivek (AE) — mutual action plan, customer liaison.
- Karthik (Platform) — infra config, perf tuning, kernel/quantization suggestions.
- Ben Carter (Solutions) — prompt engineering and eval harness.
- Irene Choi (Security) — questionnaire responses and audit evidence.

Access requirements (customer)
- S3 read-access to sample bucket (temporary role for redwood-poc@redwood.com).
- IP allowlist entry for Redwood staging cluster (list provided in the playbook).
- DocuSign MSA/POC addendum signed by procurement (Alicia Ramos).

Attachments: redwood_poc_playbook.xlsx, prompt_suite_v1.md

Action items (who / when)
- Maria: grant initial S3 access & confirm procurement contact by Monday morning.
- Alicia/Procurement: review POC addendum draft by EOD Wednesday.
- Karthik/Ben: provision staging slot and share access details before Monday kickoff.

I'll create the calendar invite for Monday 10am PT and attach the Charter and Playbook. If anything here looks off, please flag it in-thread so we can adjust before kickoff.

Thanks —
Vivek

[Attachments: redwood_poc_playbook.xlsx (xlsx), prompt_suite_v1.md (markdown)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: POC kickoff plan + owners (follow-up)

Quick internal note after reviewing the playbook:
- I'll reserve a staging GPU slab for the POC. Target instance profile: 8xA10G with mixed-precision kernels.
- Ben: want to pair on the eval harness on Tuesday 11am PT — I'll send a calendar hold.
- Irene: I'll need the set of accepted audit items so we can configure structured logging (requesting retention window & SIEM endpoint).

No changes to the customer-facing plan; just making sure we have the infra commitments on our side.
